description: Smell the flowers, listen to the birds, feel the soil and the water on your skin - the Sentier des Sens invites visitors to discover nature with all their senses.  The nature trail follows the bisse from La Tzoumaz and takes visitors back to the roots of the forest in a playful way.
itinerary: La Tzoumaz, Maison de la Forêt
La Tzoumaz, Maison de la Forêt

name: ViaValtellina, Stage 2/8
description: Route between former Walser settlements and today’s famous tourist destinations of Klosters and Davos, over the Wolfgang Pass. Visit to Kirchner Art Museum in Davos.

name: Sempachersee-Moosweg
description: From the departure point at Sursee railway station, the route soon leads through open countryside, passing peaceful meadows and fields and alongside the Sempachersee lake to Nottwil. You are in the heart of Kanton Luzern.

name: Davosersee Rundweg
description: This easy circular route leads around the superb Davosersee lake, always with wonderful views of the water, the valley and the magnificent Graubunden mountains. A worthwhile visit for nature lovers.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 9/32
description: The route follows the River Sense, then winds up to the heights with views of the Alpine peaks. Proud farmsteads in Mengestorf stand in contrast to the residential outskirts of Bern, where the old town is a UNESCO World Heritage.

name: Chemin des villages et hameaux d'Entremont
description: Splendid hike across the sunny slopes of the Val d'Entremont. The trail leads through well-preserved villages with traditional architecture and historical charm, accompanied by a wonderful view of the valley and the Mont Blanc massif.

name: Via Engiadina, Stage 7/12
description: Through the wild valleys north of Lavin and Guarda, and above the tree line on narrow paths along the steep hillside. Past rhododendron bushes and across stony hillsides. You have a magnificent view of the surrounding 3,000 m peaks. The hike ends in the ruggedly attractive town of Guarda.

name: Tour du Vallon des Vaux
description: Circular hike from Yvonand through the Vallon des Vaux nature reserve. The trail through the canyon with its imposing cliffs is very scenic. Other sights on the way include the tower of St-Martin, with magnificent views of the Jura, followed by the church of Chêne-Paquier.

name: Sentier des Statues
description: Discover the beauties of the Jura through a fantastic crest trail offering exceptional panoramic views from the Mont-Blanc to the Säntis and from the Chasseron to the Vosges. The hike ends with a path edged with tall wooden statues as well as numerous benches and a well fitted out picnic place.

name: Chemin des Bisses, Stage 3/7
description: The stage from Nendaz to Veysonnaz is a true gourmet tour. It runs through picturesque countryside in a Valais sun trap above the Rhone Valley. It follows the Grand Bisse de Vex, a historical irrigation channel that is still used. Spectacular views of the Rhone Valley make the tour a real experience.

name: Luzerner Seeuferweg
description: The route from Luzern railway station to the Hotel Seeburg leads along the promenade beside the beautiful Vierwaldstättersee (Lake Lucerne). The impressive architecture, lively activity on the stylish quay and captivating views guarantee an enjoyable outing.

name: Walserweg, Stage 15/19
description: Once upon a time, Davos was a vast expanse of woodland. Then in around 1280 AD, twelve Walser farmsteads joined two Rhaeto-Romanic farmsteads, forming what is now the popular resort of Alpenstadt. The picturesque Stafelalp was the favoured retreat of the German painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner. This route to Arosa keeps off the beaten track and boasts a magnificent mountain panorama.

name: Schabziger Höhenweg
description: Equipped with walking sticks, a hike to the «Zigerstöckli» - along a theme and discovery trail where ten stations reveal the history, makings and marketing of the famous «Glarner» Sapasago cheese (also known as Schabziger).

name: Via Calanca, Stage 2/2
description: This stage leads gently uphill into the narrow, wooded Calanca Valley. Huge moss-covered boulders lay along the trail or in the wild streams of the Calancasca. Baroque churches, impressive old buildings, vertical cliffs and a floodplain with rare amphibians line the ancient path.

name: Wageti-Rundweg
description: This popular path along the Kander offers a view of the imposing peaks around Kandersteg. It takes you past the international scout centre, elaborately decorated farmhouses and the idyllic Muggenseeli lake.

name: Senda Sursilvana, Stage 1/5
description: The route starts at the historic Oberalp Pass. From here, you’ll dip into the cultural landscape of the Surselva region. This stage is a particular delight for plant lovers. But those more interested in geology will also be drawn to the crystal-rich mountain peaks.

name: Nidwaldner Zentrumsweg, Stage 1/2
description: From Stans the route leads to the town square in Wil on the Aa River. The path continues along the Engelberg portion of the Aa and rises up to the geographical center of the canton - an attractive vantage point. Farther uphill lies the village of Niederrickenbach.

name: Promenade du côteau entre Arve et lac
description: This route from Corsier to Hermance is on the very edge of Switzerland in Canton Genève (Geneva). It reveals a picture-book landscape with vineyards, fields of flowers and glistening Lac Léman (Lake Geneva).

name: Giro del ponte tibetano
description: There are unusual sights to see above the Magadino Plain, wineries and the elaborately restored village of Curzútt among them. The hiking trail leads to the Romanesque San Bernardo church with its valuable frescoes. The suspension bridge spanning a 100 m deep ravine is sure to offer an adrenaline rush.

name: Via Alpina, Stage 3/20
description: Milk from neighbouring alps is piped to Alp Siez. On Alpine pastures are followed by a narrow ridge of black slate. The terraced alp huts on the other side of the Foopass are an architectural rarity.

name: Sentiero Lago di Lugano, Stage 2/9
description: Spectacular hike along the mountain ridge between Monte Lema and Monte Tamaro with impressive panoramic views over northern Italy, Ticino and the Alps. The Alpine and rustic Capanna Tamaro is a perfect stage point.

name: Sentiero Caprino–Cantine di Gandria
description: A hiking tour between lake and mountains in close contact with nature. At the foot of Monte Caprino the trail leads up and down through the forest and along the Lake of Lugano. Don’t forget to stop at the typical grottoes to taste Ticino specialties and also plan a visit to the Customs Museum in Cantine di Gandria.

name: Schwyzer Höhenweg, Stage 2/5
description: The route leads down the Rigi's north-eastern slope between Rigi Kulm and the ridge leading to Rigi Scheidegg. From Rigi Kulm, 13 lakes and 24 cantons can be seen. As you descend, Lake Zug, Lake Lauerz, Gnipen and Goldau, with its wildlife park, come to the fore.

name: Waldstätterweg, Stage 2/7
description: Via ladders on the Riviera - past orchards to Oberwilen and via the narrow molasse folds with ladders that at one time afforded the only overland link to Weggis. Through the Chestenenweid nature reserve via Weggis, Hertenstein and the Haldihof fruit farm to Küssnacht.

name: Liechtensteiner Panoramaweg, Stage 3/3
description: Passing Nendeln and Mauren, you pay your respects to the Schellenberg, which in 1699 became the first Herrschaft (region) to fall to the Principality of Liechtenstein. Today impressive residences line the way down into in the Rhine plain and Ruggel.

name: Schwyzer Höhenweg, Stage 1/5
description: The first stage of the Schwyzer Höhenweg (high-level trail) is a relatively short but steep hike to the highest point of the Rigi at 1,797 metres above sea level. The spectacular panoramic views, the lovely location between three lakes and the wide range of leisure activities contribute to this mountain's popularity.

name: Fribourg en diagonale, Stage 3/3
description: Start in beautifully-conserved, historic Fribourg; off the major traffic routes, through peaceful cultured landscape to the lake shore. Sightseeing attractions along the way: Greng (18th century castle) and a little further on, the obelisk commemorating the Battle of Murten.

name: Chemin de l'Areuse
description: The Romandy, the French-speaking part of Switzerland, holds many natural experiences. One leads from the charming village of Travers to Couvet in Canton Neuenburg. A stretch that promises unspoilt nature and tranquillity in the Val de Travers, which is famous for it's absinthe.

name: Kulturspur Appenzellerland, Stage 5/6
description: From Trogen, head down into the Goldachtal valley and follow its course until you reach Zweibrücken. The steep climb towards the village of Rehetobel will be rewarded with unbeatable views across Appenzellerland and the Alpstein. At the turn of the 20th century, this village was a hub for small-scale textile manufacturing. Carry on via the Kaienspitz viewpoint with its sweeping panorama, past Lake Constance and into the Alpstein mountains before going down into the Biedermeier village of Heiden.

name: Waldstätterweg, Stage 4/7
description: Crowning stage over the Renggpass - past the KKL and Triebschen estate via the Horwer peninsula at the foot of Mount Pilatus. Passage over the Renggpass, the only overland link to Obwalden in the 1860s before the construction of the Brunigstrasse.

name: Gürbe-Wildwasserweg
description: Right at the start, the view opens up towards the Gantrisch chain and the Bernese alps as the adventurous trail follows the wild Gürbe gorge. More than a hundred wooden and concrete barriers slow down the power of the torrent during the first 10 km. In the flatter lower part, where the debris is deposited, lovely bathing and barbecue areas await the visitors.

name: ViaRhenana
description: The route via the Untersee lake and Hochrhein river was for centuries Switzerland's most important waterway. Today, it follows the ViaRhenana from Kreuzlingen via Schaffhausen to Basel, through a varied landscape shaped by water.

name: Zürichsee-Rundweg, Stage 2/10
description: The route from Adliswil to Horgen is a pleasant hike along the River Sihl and over the Zimmerberg mountain. After leaving Adliswil, the path hugs the river through Langnau am Albis («Langnau a.A.» for short) and Gattikon as far as the Sihltal Zürich Uetliberg Bahn (SZU) station. From there, you leave the Sihltal valley and climb through the forest, over the Zimmerberg and then down to the lake at Horgen.

name: Thurweg, Stage 3/8
description: The canalised river Thur winds its way through the valley and past the pretty little town of Lichtensteig with its arcades. At the ruined castle at Rüdberg, there are breathtaking long-distance views of the river. You will arrive in Bütschwil via a suspension bridge, while an old wooden bridge in Lütisburg will take you back to the river Thur.

name: Rheintaler Höhenweg
description: From Bodensee through orchards and vineyards through a varying cultural landscape with castles and alps. Views of the Rhine Valley and the mountain landscape are constant companions along the Rheintaler Höhenweg.

name: ViaSbrinz, Stage 2/5
description: A challenging mountain stage over the 2207-metre-high Jochpass, the boundary between Inner Switzerland and the Bernese Oberland. The hike is enhanced by magnificent landscapes with mountain meadows, lakes and impressive peaks, above all the snow-capped Titlis.

name: ViaFrancigena, Stage 7/10
description: Just after St. Maurice you reach Vérolliez, where a small chapel commemorates the martyrdom of Saint Maurice and his companions. On the way to the Rhone Valley, you come across the famous Pissevache waterfall and the 200 metre-deep Trient Gorge.

name: ViaFrancigena, Stage 3/10
description: The poet Gilles wrote descriptions of the Venoge river. This stage from Cossonay to Saint-Sulpice is high up in some parts and follows the river in others. The pilgrimage route ultimately reaches Lake Geneva and continues to Lausanne via the Roman town of Vidy.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 2/20
description: The route leads through the Baselbiet Tafeljura along the historic Hauenstein section. Along the track, built more than 150 years ago, you can discover many original constructions. The Ergolztal and Homburgertal valleys are home to impressive castles and fortress ruins as well as Switzerland's oldest railway bridges.

name: Walserweg, Stage 1/19
description: Around 1270, the Walser people migrated from the Valais, Pomatt and Gurin over the glacial landscape of Passo del S. Bernardino to Hinterrhein. The appearance of the village is reminiscent of the times of mule-trains and waggoners.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 7/43
description:
On the ascent from Thalkirch, a superb view opens up across Beverin Nature Park. 
The people of the Safien Valley used to transport goods to the market in Ilanz via the Güner Lückli pass. In the forest above Val da Pitasch, the trail descends to the river Glenner and then climbs again to Vella.

name: Züri Oberland-Höhenweg
description: The trail leads from Winterthur through a beautiful pre-Alpine hiking area with rugged valleys, lakes and ridges with wonderful views, crowned by the highest point in Canton Zurich, the Schnebelhorn, and on to Obersee at Rapperswil with its attractive old town.

name: Unterägeri-Weg
description: This route leads you through the beautiful and open Unterägeri plain. This path through the verdant landscape with magnificent views of the Zug Oberland mountains and Ägerisee lake is a true delight.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 10/19
description: The hike through the wild Schanfigg mountain valley leads in constant ups and downs along the wooded northern slope of the Weisshorn. The deep valley that connects Chur with Arosa is a paradise for nature lovers with its sun terraces, alpine pastures and flower meadows.

name: Via Calanca, Stage 1/2
description: Between vineyards and chestnut forests, an old mule track leads to the once prosperous and influential Santa Maria. You come across drystone walls, ruins and stone buildings from various centuries on the way to the Calanca Valley. You follow the wild Calancasca river between rock faces and waterfalls.

name: Walserweg Safiental, Stage 1/3
description: The hiking trail begins in Versam. The gateway to the Safiental valley is situated above the Rhine Gorge, one of the most spectacular landscapes in the Alpine region. On the way you enjoy a panoramic view. The stage destination is Tenna, an innovative mountain village that boasts the world's first ever solar-powered ski lift.

name: Jura Crest Trail, Stage 3/16
description: Get to know five passes: Staffelegg, Bänkerjoch, Salhöhe, Schafmatt and lastly the Untere Hauenstein. In between, lots of woodland, many pastures and the rugged Geissfluh vantage point on the border of Baselland.

name: Sentier des ponts historiques du Sépey
description: This circular hike is based around three historical bridges: starting with Pont des Planches, built in 1778, there follows one road-rail bridge and the stone bridge of Pont de la Tine. The trail – which passes through woodland, a ravine and meadows – also features the church at Cergnat with its ancient belfry.
itinerary: Les Planches–Le Pont de la Tine

name: Bernina-Tour, Stage 2/5
description: On the way between Lago Bianco and Lej Nair, you will be on the language border and watershed. As you climb the rocky northern slope, the vegetation becomes sparser. At an altitude of 3,001 metres, the views of Piz Palü, Piz Bernina and the Pers and Morteratsch glaciers are breathtaking.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 14/32
description: Ridge walk on the west flank of the Pfyffer. Breathtaking views from the Wachthubel of Schrattenflue and Hohgant, foothill bastions of the Alps. Black buffalos are seen on the decent - the reason Schangnau is famous for its mozzarella.

name: Walliser Sonnenweg
description: Scenic high-level trail with panoramic views of the Valais Alps and views down into the Rhone Valley. Variety of attractions along the route: thermal spa in Leukerbad, viaducts on the Lötschberg-Südrampe, splashing water channels and the Museum of the Swiss Guard at Naters.

name: Entre Arve et Lac
description: An outing to the magnificent Genevan countryside through the vineyards between the Arve river and the lake. From Hermance, you pass through the villages of Anières, Corsier, Gy, Jussy and Lullier to reach Choulex.

name: Jöriseen Rundweg
description: This hike offers a wonderful spectacle of nature: light-green lakes set in the heart of a barren mountain landscape. Highly recommended!

name: Sentier du Balcon du Mont-Blanc
description: The trail leads from Finhaut to Six Jeur above Emosson and offers a fantastic view of the Mont Blanc Massif along the entire route. Eight information panels provide details about geology, fauna, flora and the history of the Finhaut-Emosson region.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 15/20
description: From the mountain hotel on the Schynige Platte, follow the ridge from Lütschinental to Lake Brienz. With a view of the famous snowy mountains of the Bernese Oberland or the lake down in the valley, you reach the foot of the Faulhorn via narrow mountain paths. The route down to the gondola station on the First is wider.

name: Weissenberg-Rundweg
description: This loop trail leads through the many scattered settlements on Weissenberge, a sunny mountain terrace in the Glarus region.

name: ViaSuworow, Stage 7/11
description: With views of the primeval forest reserve of Bödmeren, through which Suvorov marched in flight from the French, the route leads from Muotatal along alp trails and an impressive stone-slab path in Schluecht over the Pragelpass to Richisau in the hinteren Klöntal valley.

name: Tour des Alpes Vaudoises, Stage 3/8
description: Once you set off from the Col des Mosses pass, you will pass through expansive meadow landscapes. Surrounded by magnificent views of the Gummfluh and other peaks, this leg ends in Château-d’Oex, the main settlement in the Pays d’Enhaut district and a hub for hot air balloons.

name: Grenzpfad Napfbergland, Stage 1/6
description: The mostly flat hike across meadows and through old coniferous forests offers beautiful views of the Jura and the Napf region. The former St. Urban monastery complex, castle ruins, and the ancient water meadows bear witness to a centuries-old settlement history.

name: Aargauer Weg
description: The «Aargauer Weg» offers diversity: superb views over the foothills of the Jura and tranquil paths along the edges of river banks provide contrast with Habsburg castles, magnificent monasteries and mediaeval old towns.

name: Via Albula/Bernina, Stage 5/10
description: This leg is the highlight of the route, setting off from Preda via the Albula Pass to the southern tunnel portal. The mountain hiking trail passes by the crystal-clear Lai da Palpuogna lake, climbing up to Alp Weissenstein (known as Crap Alv in Romansh) and onward to Fuorcla Crap Alv. This is followed by a steep descent into the Val Bever valley until you reach the idyllic Spinas, your destination for this leg.

name: ViaSuworow, Stage 8/11
description: The trail leads alongside the Klöntalersee (lake) between mighty cliff faces down to Glarus. Anyone chancing a dip in the Klöntalsee may find the Russian war chest. It's reputed to have been sunk in the lake as the French attacked.

name: Kulturspur Appenzellerland
description: As you follow the six stages through archetypal hilly landscapes and gorges and over mountain ranges boasting spectacular views, you will discover the rich cultural diversity of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Picturesque remote farms and charming villages bear witness to the heyday of the local textile industry and the craftsmanship of days gone by.

name: Sentiero Lago di Lugano, Stage 1/9
description: An ideal stage to get into the hike: moderate climb, cool woodlands, an old mill converted to a grotto. Also of interest: the Museum del Malcantone at Curio and typical Ticino drystone walling along the wayside.

name: ViaValtellina, Stage 5/8
description: Surrounded by an impressive mountain landscape from Pontresina through the Val Bernina and up to the Bernina Passm watershed between the Black Sea (Lej Nair) and the Adriatic Sea (Lago Bianco). Insight into the effects of climate change in Pontresina and Morteratsch.

name: Vier-Quellen-Weg, Stage 5/5
description: The last stage of the Four Headwaters Trail climbs to the source of the Rhone. You reach the Rhone glacier with magnificent views of the Valais' four-thousand-metre peaks, accompanied by a nostalgic steam train and the serpentines of the pass road. Alpine flora thrives between large boulders.

name: ViaJura, Stage 1/7
description: A short hike out of the big city of Basel, along a medieval canal and the banks of the Birs, past Switzerland's largest football stadium and the Reinacher Heide nature reserve. Experience how nature is given space in a settlement area.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 32/43
description: Attractive trail to the Col de Mille. Intoxicating: Mont Blanc and Grand Combin massifs in the morning light. Mules graze in this area. Huge alpine pastures on the descent to Bourg St. Pierre. Napoleon and his army also spent the night here in 1800.

name: Mäderenweg
description: A tour from Rothenthurm, surrounded by a sprawling moor landscape, up to Mostelberg Mountain with fantastic views of the nearby peaks and the deep blue Aegeri Lake. The sights from the 374 meter pedestrian suspension bridge high above the Laui ravine come with an adrenalin kick.

name: Walserweg, Stage 3/19
description: Traditional or modern – wood and Vals quartzite reflect the character of Vals. The hike starts with a thrilling ascent through beautiful woodland sections, past moorland and Alp Tomül. Taking the “Polenweg”, you descend into the original Safien Valley, which is also the entrance to the Beverin Nature Park.

name: ViaJura, Stage 6/7
description: The gentle descent through the wooded, hilly Jura landscape with its impressive old trees leads past ponds, moorlands, extensive pastures and avenues of trees. Behind Tavannes, the route passes through a natural rock passage already used by the Romans.

name: Klettgau-Rhein-Weg
description: From the Hallau wine region, the route leads through the extensive forests of the Randen hill chain, over the old high-level trail to Schaffhausen. On the way: superb views from towers on the Randen and from the elevated villages of Büttenhardt and Lohn.

name: Chemin de Bellelay
description: This route through the Petit-Val holds many surprises in store. Starting at Bellelay, the cradle of the famous Tête de Moine AOP cheese, the path leads through landscapes of wooded-pastures to the impressive Pichoux Gorge. Enjoy the sweeping views of the Jura countryside and the tranquillity of the little-known valley.

name: Chemin du Val Terbi
description: The route over the hills at the very end of Val Terbi climbs up to Welschgätterli. The rocky mountain pass also forms the language border. The panoramic views of the Delémont Valley and the Basel and Solothurn regions are incredible. Several picnic areas along the way are perfect for a break.

name: Via Engiadina, Stage 3/12
description: From the Corviglia, St. Moritz’s local mountain, a narrow path leads along the steep hillside across alpine pastures high above the tree line. The view of the valley floor and the mountain peaks above Pontresina is breathtaking. The hike ends in the attractive village of Bever.

name: Kaien-St. Anton-Weg
description: Enjoy this route through the unspoilt Appenzell landscape with captivating views over the Bodensee (Lake Constance), as far as Vorarlberg and into Allgäu. Information panels along the route hold interesting facts about local medicinal plants.

name: Nationalpark-Panoramaweg, Stage 5/7
description: In the heart of the National Park the trail across Muottas Champlönch climbs down to the deep Spölschlucht gorge and back up to Fuorcla Murter. The views range far across untouched nature with valleys full of rocks and boulders, steep mountain slopes and rocky peaks. Forests of stone pine, extensive Alpine meadows and marmots make this route particularly attractive.

name: Julia Uferweg
description: In the midst of a fabulous landscape, the route leads along the river Julia to the refreshing bathing lake Lai Barnagn, which is circumnavigated. The route delights with an impressive mountain panorama and ends in Savognin with its medieval stone bridge.

name: Silvretta Gletscherlehrpfad
description: This varied hike leads to the Silvrettahütte cabin through impressive landscapes with far-reaching panoramic views of mountain peaks and Alpine flora. The Glacier Trail (Gletscherlehrpfad) sheds light on how the glacier came about and the consequences of climate change.

name: Sentier du Mont d'Or
description: The hike from Vallorbe to Mont d'Or offers an exceptional panorama: Chasseron, Suchet, Lake Neuchâtel, Joux Valley and Lake St Point.

name: Dreiland-Wanderweg, Stage 1/3
description: This stage begins with a city hike past some of Basel’s highlights. It is characterised by its alternation between city and countryside. At its end, it runs along the banks of the Birs to the destination point, Riehen Cemetery, the largest final resting place in Switzerland.

name: Senda Sursilvana, Stage 3/5
description: This stage goes past small Oberland municipalities in Grisons such as Capaul, Capeder and Casu. The Sant’Onna chapel in Trun is steeped in history. Brigels is a friendly family holiday destination. Attractive view from Adlerstein on the edge of the village.

name: Romont Stained Glass Trail
description: An undulating pathway in the heart of the Glâne’s green landscape, discovering churches and their remarkable, well-preserved, stained-glass windows. The starting point for the walk is the jewel crown of the region: the Vitromusée Romont, the Swiss Museum of Stained Glass and Glass Art.

name: ViaSurprise, Stage 6/6
description: The ascent through the wild Chälengrabe gorge leads up to the Blauenberg. The trail continues through the Aesch vineyard and alongside the Birs back to Dornach. The abbey on the station square is now devoted to culinary delights – a welcome opportunity to relive the highlights of your hike.

name: Nidwaldner Zentrumsweg, Stage 2/2
description: From Niederrickenbach it is a constant climb that eventually leads to the highest point of the hike - Buochserhorn with its wonderful panoramic views. Over alpine meadows and through shady forests, hikers pass the geographical center of central Switzerland on their way down to Buochs.

name: ViaGottardo
description: What would the Gotthard be without its access routes? The ViaGottardo reaches the central Alpine pass from Chiasso in the south, from Schaffhausen in the northeast and from Basel in the northwest of Switzerland. There are many traces of these transport links to discover along the way.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 7/33
description: After the initial ascent to Stans, impressive panoramic views open up over Stanser Boden, Lake Lucerne and the peaks of Central Switzerland. The stage's highlight at the end is the hermitage of Niklaus von Flüe with the Ranft chapels.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 6/29
description: Three cantons, two lakes and a large valley - the Linth plain - determine the characteristics of this crossover stage from Eastern to Central Switzerland. In addition, it offers a historic stairway, a lakeside promenade and lots of level countryside.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 18/19
description: From the monastery village of Disentis/Mustér, this stage leads through small farming villages, and past the Sogn Giachen chapel in Cuoz, which was built by the Brotherhood of St. James. On the mountain path, you can enjoy the view of the Vorderrhein, which winds through the valley. You cross the 120-metre-long railway viaduct at Bugnei.

name: Nationalpark-Panoramaweg
description: Experience 7 days of the pristine environment in the rugged canyons and on the steep mountain slopes in and around the Swiss National Park. At an altitude of 2,945 m, the trail leads along smugglers’ paths through tunnels in the rocks. Dense mountain forests, expansive Alpine pastures and the vibrant colours of mountain lakes and Alpine flowers are a delight to see.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 17/43
description: A varied stage, with panoramic scenery throughout: Alpine climb to Bortelhütte, blueberry picking above Rothwald in autumn. The trail leads along the pass road gallery from Schallbett to the Simplonpass.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 5/20
description: From the Jura heights with its many views between Magglingen and Evilard, the path descends into the wild Taubenloch Gorge. Bridges and tunnels enable you to go right into the residential area of Bözingen. Along the Suze and through Biel, this stage ends at the train station via the shore of the lake.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 2/43
description: Fuorcla d’Agnel is the name of the pass on this stage, which is the gateway to Parc Ela. Alp Flix, the high plateau that is this hike's destination, is one of the many gems in Switzerland's largest regional nature park. It is also dubbed the "Treasure Island of Biodiversity".

name: Urnersee-Uferweg
description: On water or on land - this is an inspiring route thanks to stunning views of the Urnersee lake, the southern arm of the Vierwaldstättersee (Lake Lucerne), embedded in a magnificent mountain panorama and surrounded by an opulent, generously renatured plant world.

name: Via Capricorn
description: Split into three day-long stages, the Via Capricorn leads across ibex country on the slopes of the Schamserberg and right through the middle of Beverin Nature Park. You can discover the area’s rich alpine flora, unique geology and the original Walser culture, all on foot.

name: Chemin de la Grande Cariçaie
description: Nature and humans live together harmoniously in the Grande Cariçaie on the southern shore of Lake Neuchâtel. The nature reserve, Switzerland's largest lakeside wetland, is home to 800 plant species and over 10,000 animal species, who shape the banks under the friendly gaze of passing hikers.

name: Dreiland-Wanderweg, Stage 3/3
description: The impressive harbour facilities and the Three Countries Bridge mark the international location of this stage. In the Krebsbachtal Nature Reserve, you can explore the habitat of many plant and animal species. In Friedlingen, you can find out about the important history of textiles.

name: Walserweg, Stage 12/19
description: The long hike begins at 2,252 metres of elevation, descending through Val Spadlatscha to Filisur. Running past typical Engadine houses, the spectacular hiking trail passes through scree and avalanche paths that extend from the Muchetta massif down to the Landwasser river. You can enjoy a stunning view of the Wiesen Viaduct, the largest brick-built bridge on the Rhaetian Railway.

name: Rheintaler Höhenweg, Stage 2/6
description: From the Meldegg, with wide-ranging views over the lower Rhine Valley and to Hohen Kasten, through a typical Appenzell region, past the Grünenstein castles in the Riesling-Silvaner wine region – with “Gilde” culinary highlights.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 8/19
description: From the seclusion of Alp Dürrboden, you hike through the Dischma Valley into the vibrant, highest situated town in the Alps. Or from the lovely Alpine huts to large concrete buildings. The mountain scenery and charming streams remain captivating from start to finish.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 4/32
description: Across lush meadows, between mighty fir trees to «Energy Mountain» and the wind farm with its rotating propellers, visible from afar, and solar panels: Switzerland’s largest plant for renewable energy! Then a steep descent to St-Imier.

name: Thurweg, Stage 4/8
description: From the beautiful bridge viaduct, the walk follows the straightened course of the River Thur. Red kites searching for food can be spotted, while information boards and gnawed trees provide insights into the beaver population that lives here. Riverside forests, historical bridges and the beautiful old town of Bischofszell are yet more highlights of this flat stage.

name: Wysswasser-Weg
description: An excursion from Fiesch to the Fieschertal - always alongside the lively  Wysswasser river - is the purest of natural experiences. Here the mountain landscape of the Valais is presented at it's best. It's impossible to do anything but relax and enjoy it.

name: Sentier du Lac de la Gruyère, Stage 2/3
description: This stage is rich in history, including the stately Vuippens with its castle and gardens, the isle of Ogoz and its vestiges of mediaeval life. Along the shore, you can enjoy bathing, water sports or fine food, before returning to Rossens along the path that overlooks the lake and the molasse cliffs.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 9/33
description: Brünig boasts views of an impressive mountain panorama, featuring the high peaks of the Bernese Oberland and snow all year round. The route crosses sunny valley slopes above the shimmering turquoise waters of Lake Brienz, surrounding you with extraordinarily beautiful scenery.

name: Aussichtsweg Morteratschgletscher
description: This trip offers exceptional views of the crevasseriven Morteratsch Glacier and of the ice-capped peaks of the Bernina massif. Along the way, 16 information panels illustrate the retreat of the glacier.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 38/43
description: This unofficial lower Valais "high route" leads from the Lac d'Emosson across two passes to the Lac de Salanfe, at an altitude of 1900 to 2500 metres. Along the way, water and rock, flowers and snow alternate in a varied succession.

name: Waldstätterweg, Stage 3/7
description: Stroll with views of the Alps - from Küssnacht through the nature reserves in Wagenmoos, along the lakeshore at Meggen and Meggehorn castle. Approach to the city of Lucerne and arrival along the 19th-century tourism alley, its quay with distant views of the Alps.

name: Gommer Höhenweg
description: This hiking path on the sunny side of the upper Rhone Valley offers fantastic views of the snow-capped peaks of the 4000 m mountains in the Valais. The trails meander through the fascinating landscape of the Obergoms with flower-covered meadows and fragrant larch forests.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 7/19
description: From traditional Engadin architecture into the beautiful, secluded Val Susauna: a long, thrilling climb leads you to the two Alps Pignaint and Funtauna. A trail ascends 2,605 metres up to the Scaletta Pass. This is followed by the descent into the Dischma Valley towards Dürrboden, surrounded by a glorious mountain backdrop.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 24/32
description: A steep mountain trail leads from the legendary Swiss Alpine pass down to the Leventina Valley. A spectacular Alpine landscape combined with amazing construction achievements from different eras and in close vicinity of the Tremola, a road with landmark designation.

name: Dreiland-Wanderweg
description: With a detour into the neighbouring country, this route is taking a wide arc around Basel. The hike is marked by impressions along the Rhine, variety in the Markgräfler vineyard region and constantly changing views of the city.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 5/29
description: The rather long ascent from Stein to Vorder Höhi is finally rewarded with wonderful views of the Glarner mountain peaks. A diverse high-level hike leads around the Gulme, across to the Mattstogg and down to Amden.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 1/20
description: From Bellelay, this stage leads along the peat bog of La Sagne. Through forests and across pastures, it climbs up to the gentle Jura height, where you remain for a few kilometres. The path descends across open pastures to the destination for the first stage, the village of Tramelan.

name: Chemin de Montoz
description: This hike starts at Untergrenchenberg and explores the Montoz ridge. The summit is a hilly plateau, surrounded by a broad forest belt. The views from the Montoz extend all the way to the Alps, if the weather is clear.

name: Schijenfluh Umrundung
description: This cross-border hiking tour into nearby Austria not only allows us to retrace the footsteps of the Walser people and many a smuggler, it also provides a geological cross-section through the Rätikon mountain range with its striking contrast of light limestone and dark crystalline Silvretta rock.

name: Sentier des Gorges de l'Areuse
description: Sometimes wide, sometimes narrow, sometimes gurgling and thundering, sometimes gently babbling: the Areuse river. This charming route follows the constantly surprising river. Old stone bridges, footbridges and steps, crevices and impressive rock faces characterise the walk in the heart of narrow, refreshing gorges.

name: Nationalpark-Panoramaweg, Stage 6/7
description: Through beautiful stone pine forests and across wild scree gullies in rugged Val Cluozza on the way to Piz Murtaröl. The views from the ridge of Piz Terza in the east and the crevasses and peaks of the National Park in the south are incredible, and abundant wildlife can be spotted on the steep slopes.

name: Obwaldner Höhenweg, Stage 3/6
description: The popular Schönbüel-Brünigpass route is a feast for all the senses and is not short of gorgeous views. Along the way, the Gibel mountain will serve as your spectacular front-row seat, with views of Lake Brienz and Lake Thun below. Then comes a ridge walk towards the Wilerhorn, before the route leads down through woodland and meadows to the Brünig Pass.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 23/32
description: Follow the footsteps of the muleteers from Andermatt to the Gotthard Pass on the centuries-old north-south axis. The route along the Reuss through the romantic Urseren Valley to Hospental is mostly flat. From there, climb the historic mule trail to Switzerland’s most important Alpine pass, accompanied by the burbling Gotthard-Reuss River.

name: Via Albula/Bernina, Stage 2/10
description: The second leg takes you to one of the highlights of the entire route: the imposing Landwasser Viaduct. But first you will walk along the burbling river Albula, past the central point of the canton of the Grisons and onward to one of the photo opportunities for taking a souvenir picture of the world-famous Rhaetian Railways viaduct.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 1/19
description: Müstair with St. Johann UNESCO World Heritage Site is your starting point for the leg over Sta. Maria, Valchava through the larch woods bordering the National Park, to Fuldera and Tschierv. And from the highest Ofenpass village over an upwards trail to Lü.

name: Jura Crest Trail, Stage 16/16
description: A bleak rock bastion and the lush Lac Léman shores: a pair of contrasts on this tour. After climbing to the top of La Dôle near the national border, the trail leads through forests to vineyards and Nyon, a small town in a superb location.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 29/33
description: Hiking from Bern (Bärengraben) to Rüeggisberg you continually catch glimpses of the snow-capped trio of the Eiger Mönch & Jungfrau above the forest.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 39/43
description: At first, the route leads steadily up to the Col de Susanfe with a magnificent view of the Dents du Midi. The Cabane de Susanfe, a classic SAC mountain hut from 1930, is set in the midst of green meadows. From there, the descent to the Val d'Illiez is quite steep.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 27/32
description: The most romantic but steepest section of the Strada alta trail. The old mule trail leads over rocky spurs and through tranquil chestnut forests to the unique open-air steps above Pollegio. A spurt to the finish at Biasca down in the Leventina Valley.

name: Höhenweg Maderanertal
description: The valley of Maderanertal, world famous due to its natural beauty, opens up in Amsteg and the towering peak of Chli Windgällen and winds itself east ways towards the imposing Huefi glacier, always surrounded by high alpine mountain peaks.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 3/20
description: An old pass trail leads over the Unteren Hauenstein to Olten. Thanks to the basis tunnel, only the S-Bahn trains now run on the scenically-rewarding section over the pass. The views from the Hauenstein can thus be enjoyed in peace.

name: Siebenbrunnen-Weg
description: The hike to the Simmen waterfalls, to the "seven fountains", and on via Langermatte to Iffigenalp is one of the most popular in Lenk. It takes the visitors to the most beautiful water spectacles of the Simmen valley and offers a magnificent view of the surrounding mountains and the village of Lenk.

name: Appenzeller Weg, Stage 3/3
description: The route begins in tradition-steeped Urnäsch and passes through the historic textile area of Schönengrund before ending in St. Peterzell. The last section leads through the gentle rolling landscape and crosses the cantonal border from the Apenzell region to St. Gallen.

name: Geopfad Wiriehorn
description: About 3.5 hours takes the round trip hike around the monument of the Diemtigal. On the mountain trail around the Wiriehorn you get the best panoramic view into the Diem-tigtal. A nice opportunity to end the hike is to drive down to the valley with a Trottinet.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 26/33
description: Between the Lucerne hinterland and the Bernese Oberemmental, the trail leads away from traffic over hills and through wooded areas to Ufhusen and Huttwil. Picturesque farms and panoramic views of the Alps and, later, the Jura accompany the hikers.

name: Brienzersee Drei Wasserfälleweg, Stage 1/2
description: From Bönigen the trail leads alongside the lake, turning right towards the forest after about 1 km. You reach the light-flooded waterfall Eschwanden along a narrow forest path. The hike continues through the forest and alongside a cliff face where you reach the pilgrims' path and the Fura above Iseltwald.

name: ViaFrancigena
description: Established 2000 years ago, in medieval times the ViaFrancigena became the most important pilgrims’ path in Europe. In Switzerland it leads through beautiful Jura and Alpine landscapes, the stage on the Grossen St. Bernhard being particularly magnificent.

name: Chemin du Jura bernois, Stage 2/4
description: The enjoyable hike over the hills of the Jura leads through wetlands, past attractive ancient trees and across wide pastures with a view of the Chasseral. On the way you see drystone walls, stud horses, tree-lined roads and baroque churches, and you pass the place where Tête de Moine cheese was invented.

name: Flimspitz-Rundweg
description: A hike around the Flimspitz and past five beautiful clear lakes. The trail crosses the terrain of Alp Trida with countless boulders left behind after a rock fall. The backdrop: the peaks of the three-country corner of Switzerland - Austria - Italy.

name: Giro delle Rovine del Castelliere
description: A thrilling hike to the prehistoric Castelliere castle ruins above Tegna, with spectacular views of Lake Maggiore, the Centovalli and extending as far as Italy. Past the impressive Orrido Gorge, you follow the Maggia to Ponte Brolla.

name: Chemin du 100e du CAS Jura
description: A delightful hike from St-Ursanne to Lucelle, the first of six stages of the Ajoie Circuit created to mark the 100th anniversary of the Jura section of Swiss Alpine Club (SAC). Discover magnificent landscapes along this exciting and challenging route.

name: Seeland-Solothurn-Weg, Stage 1/4
description: The stage along the lakeshore to the bilingual town of Biel/Bienne offers flowering shrubs in spring, tranquil nature in autumn and numerous swimming opportunities in summer. Picturesque Erlach is the starting point.

name: Seeland-Solothurn-Weg, Stage 4/4
description: This stage leads along the Emme's lovely, secluded riverside path to Solothurn on the Aare. Industrial buildings contrast with opportunities to spend time by the water. In Solothurn, by its own account, Switzerland's most beautiful baroque town, numerous sights await you.

name: Bürgenstock-Weg
description: «Stunning» must be the most apt description for this route. Located at the heart of Central Switzerland, high above the picturesque Vierwaldstättersee (Lake Lucerne) and with the best views of the Alpine peaks, the Bürgenstock leaves nothing to be desired.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 10/29
description: After a pleasant ramble alongside the Zugersee lake, you reach the first highlight – the vantage point of Michaelskreuz with restaurant and wedding chapel. Following an undulating stretch you reach Dietschiberg, where you can watch golf at close quarters.

name: Chemin du Lac de Morat
description: The small medieval town of Murten, with its lake shore directly before the town walls, offers an especially scenic route around the Murtensee lake. The appealing lakeside promenade, vineyards and the historic old town is a must for romanticists!

name: Hochtal Val Frisal
description: The Val Frisal Plateau is one of the most beautiful high valleys of the Alps. A wide view of the valley shows a vast floodplain with branching rivers. The Scatlé ancient spruce forest is another highlight of this hike.

name: Via Alpina, Stage 9/20
description: Through Alpine flora to Tannalp with dairy, inn and lake. The ridge hike over Balmeregghorn, with wonderful views of the Eiger, Mönch & Jungfrau is truly impressive. Muggenstutz the dwarf and a sculpture garden promise variety on the way to Meiringen.

name: WALSA-Weg, Stage 3/4
description: The Flumserberg, considered the centrepiece of Heidiland, enjoys long hours of sunshine and magnificent views of the Churfisten mountain range and Lake Walen. The initial section is followed by a mule track through rocks and roots. Once you reach Chnobelboden, hike along the west-facing slope through open terrain studded with houses and bustling with agricultural activity.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 16/19
description: From Andiast, this stage leads to sun-drenched Brigels, which sits on a high plateau with its houses that are browned by the sun, the historic village centre and the stunning Lake Brigels. With a view of the Vorderrhein, you cross alpine meadows and mountain streams until you arrive in historic Trun.

name: Blauburgunderland Panoramaweg
description: The hiking trail up in the heights that leads through the heart of Schaffhausen's Blauburgunderland. The route goes along a mountain ridge that extends to the southeast. The focus of this route is the Mediterranean-like views of the vineyards of Blauburgunderland.

name: Aletsch Panoramaweg, Stage 3/3
description: The trail follows old Alpine paths down to the Burg, a rock massif of gneiss smoothed by glaciers. Against the backdrop of the Goms mountains, the Fiescher Glacier becomes clearly visible. The 160-metre-long Aspi-Titter suspension bridge points the way to the idyllic Goms mountain village of Bellwald.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 24/29
description: A pleasant hike through the steep Lavaux vineyards, a UNESCO World Heritage since 2007. Along the way you meet the old traditional wine villages of St-Saphorin, Rivaz and Epesses, and the lovely little towns of Cully and Lutry on Lac Léman.

name: Furi-Weg
description: This route from Furi down to  Zermatt village offers views of the region's stunning scenery, always accompanied by the impressive Matterhorn. The untouched landscape surrounded by a magnificent mountain world is a true feast for the eyes.

name: Uferweg Stein am Rhein
description: The round tour in Stein am Rhein will raise the pulse of nature lovers and fans of medieval times in equal measure. The route leads along the picturesque banks of the Rhine and holds many attractions at the ready.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 3/32
description: A climb to the high plateau of the Franches Montagnes and peaceful countryside. Dark forests and scattered farmsteads surrounded by horses, cattle and sheep. In between, villages with mustard-coloured houses. Saigneléger is the regional centre.

name: Walserweg Gottardo, Stage 9/14
description: Going up steeply through the barrier woodland, then on a high path with a wonderful view across the Bedretto Valley towards the Gotthard Pass. Also in view: a wide variety of transport systems that tell the history of the development of the most important Swiss Alpine pass, including the famous Tremolastrasse. It is considered to be the longest architectural monument in Switzerland.

name: Eiger Trail
description: The Eiger North Wall is close enough to touch from the Eiger Trail and the various world-famous climbing routes to the notorious Eiger summit are easy to spot.

name: ViaSuworow, Stage 4/11
description: The wonderful cultural landscapes with medieval buildings and stone arch bridges are a joy to behold along the route through the lower Reusstal valley. Totally in contrast to Suvorov and his troops, who only had French soldiers in sight.

name: ViaSuworow, Stage 3/11
description: Taking the route through the Schöllenenschlucht gorge today is much easier than in Suvorov's time. He and his soldiers had to force the French troops back down the valley. However, he was given a memorial at the Teufelsbrücke (Devil's Bridge) for his pains.

name: Stockhorn-Panoramaweg
description: This hike is the classic route in the Stockhorn region. On the diverse route you can enjoy special, exciting views. The start and end of the route are the mountain and middle stations of the Stockhornbahn railway.

name: Margelchopf-Gipfelweg
description: This hike leads across meadows and alps to Margelchopf, the imposing local mountain of Grabs. The grassy high plateau invites you to linger with its impressive view across the St. Gallen Rhine Valley and as far as Lake Constance. At the end, you can cool down in Lake Voralp.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 20/32
description: This stage leads down to Seedorf following the Swiss Path (Weg der Schweiz), which comes from Rütli and leads via Flüelen to Brunnen. The whole route and the Rütli are visible on the descent to Bauen. Interesting small castles and mansions along the route.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 30/33
description: On this leg of the journey, you can recharge your batteries in the tranquillity of nature. The route connects Fribourg, founded by the House of Zähringen, with Payerne, a town created by Queen Bertha. Along the way, you will enjoy enchanting woodland, an idyllic spot to rest by the river, rural villages and a mini-enclave with a church of pilgrimage.

name: Wilket-Gratweg
description: From Brunnadern you climb through the forest up to Wilkethöchi, highest point of this tour and panoramic highlight. The views of the Alpstein mountain range and the Alps of the Glarus region are spectacular. Two short climbs follow after the village of Dicken, in addition to two mountain inns with lovely views, before the path begins to descend via the Bruderwald forest to Degersheim.

name: Tour du Lac de Joux
description: Featuring three mountain lakes, Nordic landscapes, watchmaking and culinary specialties, Joux Valley has been an attractive region for all lovers of nature and authenticity for many years. This hike leads around Lac de Joux, the largest lake in the Jura massif.

name: Thurweg, Stage 8/8
description: The eighth stage of the Thurweg trail runs on well-maintained and natural paths that extend along a meadow landscape. It initially follows the course of the Thur, which later flows into the Rhine. The destination for the stage, Rüdlingen, is an exclave of the canton of Schaffhausen.

name: Chemin des villages d’Evolène
description: Initially along the Borgnes river, then up into the villages high on the cliffs. Typical homes, barns and chapels are found around Evolène in a protected landscape with views across the mountains and the untamed Val d’Hérens. And finally, a section of the trail with paintings and poetry.

name: Freiburger Voralpenweg, Stage 4/5
description: A mysterious waterfall, a beautiful forest path and imposing limestone rock faces are the defining features of this leg from Jaun to the Chalet du Soldat. Your destination for this leg is in a magnificent spot with far-reaching views of the Gastlosen mountain range and numerous peaks of the Fribourg Prealps.

name: Vier-Quellen-Weg
description: The Vier-Quellen-Weg (Four Headwaters Trail) in the Gotthard Massif leads to the sources of four rivers: the Rhine, Reuss, Ticino and Rhone. A tour through an exceptional Alpine landscape with a wide diversity of fauna, flora and witnesses to a historic past.

name: Via Albula/Bernina, Stage 4/10
description: This mountain hiking trail gives you a tour of a real masterpiece of engineering, following the bank of the river Albula and crossing the railway line multiple times in a section that demonstrates the boldest possible track design. The Railway Adventure Trail reveals the ingenuity behind this century-old piece of railway engineering.

name: Schanfigger Höhenweg
description: The Schanfigger Höhenweg is a journey through time and a spectacle of nature at the same time. On old mule tracks, the mountain path leads from the holiday resort of Arosa to the Alpine city of Chur. Through the Schanfigg with its picturesque side valleys Sapün and Fondei, you walk across sunny plateaus, explore original Walser settlements and rugged canyons.

name: Trutg dil Flem – Flimser Wasserweg
description: From the UNESCO World Heritage site of Sardona the new Trutg dil Flem trail follows the Flem stream from Segnesboden, past bizarre rock formations and breathtaking gorges through Europe's largest landslide to Flims.

name: Via Albula/Bernina, Stage 6/10
description: In the secluded Bever Valley, the path follows the Beverin mountain stream through larch forests. Later it continues upstream along the Inn with views of the Bernina massif. Through the renatured river landscape along the Rhaetian Railway the route leads to the exclusive holiday resort of St. Moritz.

name: Walserweg, Stage 6/19
description: Climb to the scenic vantage point of Burg Hohenrätien (castle) and the prehistoric rock drawings at Crap Carschenna. Up a narrow trail to the forest clearing at Crocs. Flower-filled hay meadows on Muttner Berg. Typical Walser settlement of Obermutten with tiny timber church.

name: Via Alpina, Stage 20/20
description: From Rochers de Naye, rock-restaurant and panorama of hundreds of crags and summits, the route leads along a steep ridge and sandstone cliff trail, later down over Mediterranean hills to Montreux.

name: Lauras Lieblingsplätze
description: Laura the Goat is centre-stage on this tour of the environs of Gais. Hike through the moorlands with views of the hill country as you pass Laura's favourite spots: an idyllic lakelet, goat sheds, a training track for goat kids, and seats with views of Mount Säntis.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 15/19
description: Ladir, Ruschein and Siat are located high above the bottom of the valley and offer views of the Piz Mundaun excursion mountain. After the Siater Alp, the path leads steeply down to the depiction of St. James in the church of St. Valentin in Pigniu/Panix. The destination for this stage is Andiast.

name: Furka-Höhenweg, Stage 2/2
description: Pleasant hike on Urschnen high-level trail along stony south-eastern slopes above Urserental. Views down to Realp and Hospental, pass road and historic Furka steam railway. En route: tiny lakes, Alpine flowers, mountain streams and jagged cliffs.

name: Wiesenweg
description: The departure point for this route is the Badische Bahnhof railway station in Basel. The Lange Erlen wildlife park, the Dammweg along the river and the open landscape in Riehen ensure a varied and unforgettable tour.

name: Neckerweg
description: Following the entire length of the river Necker from its headwaters to its mouth, this route sets off from the Schwägalp Pass in the foothills of the Säntis before arriving at the river. You will follow its course to St. Peterzell, which is on the Way of St. James, and continue through a protected floodplain area where the Necker flows into the river Thur near Lütisburg.

name: Romanshorn-Rundweg
description: This circular hike in the glorious landscape beside Lake Constance leads through shaded woodlands, vibrant fields alive with colours and along the shore of the lake, making for an unforgettable experience in the great outdoors. Historical buildings, charming harbours and magnificent views make this journey complete.

name: Höhenweg Elsigenalp–Adelboden
description: This scenic and varied hike in the heart of the Bernese Oberland undulates over various different Alps. The High-Altitude Trail (Höhenweg) with its 180-degree mountain panorama into the Engstligental valley and all its further reaches is suitable for all the family.

name: Chemin de la Sarine au Pays-d'Enhaut
description: From Rougemont, which was once the priory of Cluny, the trial goes over the Kirchenhügel from Château-d'Oex to the Grand Chalet of Rossinière. It goes between the rushing Saane and landscape steeped in history, moulded by the mountain farmers.

name: Aletsch Panoramaweg
description: Three days under the spell of the Valais glacier landscape. Sensational scenic tour with many vantage points onto the two longest glaciers in the Alps. The grey-white of ice and rock contrasting with shades of green in the Aletschwald (forest) provides stunning scenic beauty.

name: Circuito Dongio-Satro
description: An excursion that unfolds in the municipality of Acquarossa (in the middle of the Valle di Blenio), on the banks of the Brenno river through wetlands of great natural beauty. An area of great landscape and cultural importance, with typical local gastronomic and artisanal products.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 15/29
description: The route leads through the heart of the Emmental via a long mountain crest with scattered farmsteads and varying views down into the wide valley of the Grosse Emme, then on up to the equally scenic Moosegg.

name: Giro della Valle del Salto
description: Hiking on historical footpaths in the untouched Valle del Salto near Maggia. In the shade of birches and chestnut trees, you pass the region’s typical country-style homes and pretty churches, including a votive chapel with frescoes by Giovanni Antonio Vanoni.

name: Sentiero del Monte Generoso
description: From the Apennine Mountains to the Alps – the panoramic view from Monte Generoso is one of the most spectacular in Switzerland. “Fiore di Pietra” designed by architect Mario Botta is another highlight. Distinctive features of this area are the nevère, cylindrical stone structures once used to store milk.

name: Circuito di Lodano
description: This trail connects the picturesque Ticino villages of Lodano and Maggia. It runs across fields, through lush forests and past vineyards and small, typical stone houses. You keep catching a glimpse of the crystal blue Maggia River, which winds through the Maggia Valley surrounded by striking peaks.

name: Rotten-Weg Bitsch–Lalden
description: The popular Red Mile from Bitsch to Brig offers glorious panoramic views over the Rhone Valley and the Alps surrounding it. The hiking trail from Brig leads through the colourful landscape along the river Rhone to Lalden. The river landscape and mountains of Valais are sure to make for an unforgettable hiking experience.

name: Neckerweg, Stage 2/2
description: Setting off from the monastery village of St. Peterzell in Toggenburg, this hiking route then passes through an animal sanctuary, entices you to take a refreshing dip in the river Necker and winds through a protected floodplain area of national importance.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 36/43
description: This relatively short stage is part of the "Tour du Mont Blanc". After the romantic, uninhabited Durnand valley comes a steep climb to Alp Bovine, where magnificent views of the Rhone Valley and Martigny beckon.

name: Gamplüt-Säntis-Weg
description: This is a tour for those who like uphill hiking: The path first crosses a colourful sea of flowers all the way to Alp Tesel, then zigzags higher and higher across Zwingli Pass and Rotstein Pass. You can see the destination far ahead, before the route ends via Lisengrat on Mt. Säntis, the most prominent mountain in Eastern Switzerland.

name: Arosa-Ochsenalp Rundtour
description: The big star of this hike is the diverse landscape around Arosa. From the highest point, the «Hauptichopf» peak, you can enjoy the splendid panorama of the Schanfigg and Rhine Valleys near Chur. Due to its convenient location, the trail is accessible from spring onwards and a popular early-season route.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 19/29
description: From the Bernese village of Guggisberg down to the sleepy hamlet of Hirschmatt; via forested hills to the rugged Sensegraben at Zollhaus, into Canton Fribourg and alongside the Warme Sense to the holiday centre of Schwarzsee.

name: Vier-Seen-Wanderung
description: Fabulous mountain scenery around mighty Mount Titlis, unique flora, the crystal-clear waters of Lakes Melch, Tannen, Engstlen and Trüb – this route linking Melchsee-Frutt and Engelberg is justly rated as one of the classic high-altitude hikes.

name: Appenzeller Alpenweg, Stage 1/2
description: This trail takes you to the alpine foothill landscape of Appenzellerland, from Urnäsch to Alpweiden at the foot of Säntis and Schwägalp. From the Hochalp to the Schwägalp you will walk through the Schwägalp natural park, a protected natural site with a very special appeal.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 1/20
description: From the urban banks of the Rhine to the green hilly landscape of the Basel region: The first stage of the ViaGottardo takes you through the lively centre of Basel along the renaturalised banks of the Bir and combines forests, orchards, ruined castles and historic village centres with far-reaching views into Alsace and to the Vosges mountains.

name: Nidwaldner Höhenweg, Stage 3/6
description: Past four wonderful mountain lakes and over the Jochpass to the monastery village of Engelberg. The nearby imposing mountain world of the Hochstollen, Glogghuis and Titlis bids you welcome. The long descent to Engelberg can be shortened with the aerial cableway.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 18/20
description: A challenging trail leads from Paradiso up to San Salvatore, Lake Lugano's most famous vantage point. Past picturesque landscapes and hospitable grotti, the ridge hike heads south through the forest and ends in a long, winding stone staircase to Morcote.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 21/33
description: The hike begins at Konstanz Minster and takes you over the Seerücken ridge into the Thurtal valley. St. Jakob’s Church in Märstetten is a stop on the pilgrims’ way from Konstanz to Einsiedeln, a well-known feeder route to the Way of St. James that is also known as the «Schwabenweg», or «Swabian Way».

name: Schanfigger Höhenweg, Stage 4/6
description: The fourth stage of the Schanfigger Höhenweg continues over old mule tracks across the Strela, Casanna and Duranna passes. The contrast between the bleak Alpine landscape and the Fondei mountain valley with its peaceful grass slopes, dry meadows and scattered Walser houses could not be greater. The tour begins with a long ascent up to Wasserscheidi and then dips down into the gorgeous Fondei high valley.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 28/29
description: Leaving the traffic congestion of the built-up area along the lake shore, the hiking path swings into the flat hinterland between Lac Lèman and the Jura, with sleepy villages, old castles, sparkling streams, airy oak woods and cultivated fields.

name: ViaValtellina, Stage 1/8
description: From Montafon over the Alpine pastures of Valzifenz and the 2202m-high Schlappiner Joch to the former Walser settlement of Schlappin in Prättigau. Interesting introduction to the history of Montafon in the Schruns Local History Museum.

name: Walserweg Gottardo, Stage 4/14
description: Running steeply across the Passo di Nefelgiù, along wild stream ditches and onwards into the next pieces of terrain. Lake Morasco, the ancient Walser settlement of Riale and the impressive Toce waterfall are on the descent into Val Formazza. The destination for this stage in the valley is Ponte or Zum Schtäg, as it is known in Walser German.

name: Emme-Uferweg
description: This popular hiking and cycling trail starts in Burgdorf and runs for its whole length alongside the River Emme to Hasle bei Burgdorf. The route is ideal for tanking up on energy and total relaxation in beautiful surroundings.

name: Nidwaldner Höhenweg, Stage 6/6
description: This stage leads you on the famous «Wildbeobachtungspfad» (wildlife-watching trail) along the Schwalmis and Oberbauen mountain flanks to Niderbauen and the cableway summit station of the same name.

name: Sentiero del Monte Bar
description: This walk passes two of the most beautiful viewpoints of the region: Motto della Croce and Monte Bar in Val Colla. With Lugano and surroundings below, the views range all the way to Milan in good weather. This alone is worth the steep ascent over meadows, alps and through forests.

name: Wildenstein – Rifenstein Weg
description: A romantic walk on a plateau bordered by cherry trees in the Basel region, taking the walker back to the Middle Ages with a visit to the castle of Schloss Wildenstein. The last third of the walk overlaps with the path of the Erlebnisweg Titterten and the Rifensteiner Sagenweg.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 11/43
description: From alpine hut to alpine hut: first, a pleasant hike to the Passo di Gana Negra with its pitch-black rocks, green meadows and small streams. Then a steep descent and an ascent across a high plateau to the Passo delle Columbe with views of several 4000-metre peaks. Your destination is the Capanna Cadagno above lake Ritom.

name: Pfäffikersee-Rundweg
description: This is popular circular route around the Pfäffikersee lake in the Zürcher Oberland. It leads through exceptionally attractive nature, with typical moorland flora, passing the romantic farming village of Seegräben and back to the lively lake promenade at Pfäffikon ZH.

name: Chemin du Jura, Stage 1/5
description: The scenic path through the hilly, wooded Jura landscape runs mainly along a ridge and ends at the Etang de Lucelle on the French border. At Les Ordons, the views over the Jura chain, the Alps, the Black Forest, the upper Rhine valley, the Vosges and part of Franche-Comté are magnificent.

name: Sentier Panorama 4000
description: Panoramic hike above Crans-Montana. The main attraction: the magnificent view of the 4000-metre mountain range and the Rhone valley. Another scenic highlight is the section in the Tièche valley.

name: Aargauer Weg, Stage 4/6
description: From Brugg, climb up to the Gebenstorfer Horn, the perfect viewing platform for the Switzerland's «Wasserschloss». Along the Jura ridgeway to Baldegg with views of the Alps, then down to the former Habsburg Stein Castle and down to the beautiful Baden old town.

name: A la riva dal Rom
description: A hike along the banks of the wild Rom, the main valley river in the Val Müstair. From its source to Müstair, the path meanders through a lovely river landscape with floodplains, gravel banks and flowering meadows. Information boards and a brochure offer insights into the eventful history, special habitats or legends associated with the Rom.

name: ViaBerna
description: The Via Berna presents a cross-section of the diverse canton of Bern. From the gentle hills on the edge of the Franches-Montagnes, it crosses the highest Jura fold. Along the Aare to Lake Thun, across several Alpine passes and on mountain trails with incredible views, you can reach Susten Pass in 20 stages.

name: ViaJura, Stage 7/7
description: The trail follows the Suze through gorges and deep valleys on its way from the hilly, forested Jura to the lively city of Biel. Through narrow tunnels in the rock and under the pillars of the roads, you can see how deeply the river has cut into the 150-million-year-old rock.

name: Via Alpina, Stage 11/20
description: The climb to Kleine Scheidegg over undulating meadows is gentle, the rock and ice scenery of the Eiger North Wall close and awe-inspiring. Sunny high-level trail to Wengen, then deep into the Lauterbrunnen Valley with its vertical walls and spectacular waterfalls.

name: Mittelbünden-Panoramaweg
description: This tour offers an interesting cross section from Lenzerheide through the Schanfigg to Davos. Geology takes priority on the first section, whilst the second follows the footsteps of the Walser settlers. And in the middle, the tourist resort of Arosa beckons.

name: Sardona-Welterbe-Weg, Stage 4/6
description: Through wild, rocky valleys with views of pretty mountain lakes and spectacular geological phenomena, the trail climbs over 1,300 metres in altitude. The Batöni waterfall arena, a narrow suspension bridge and families of marmots and ibexes enliven the hike.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 6/33
description: This stage includes a boat trip from Brunnen to Treib, where the cantons of Uri, Schwyz and Nidwalden meet. The chapels along the way and the Winkelried monument in Stans are worth seeing.

name: Moosalp Panoramaweg
description: If you don't know Moosalp yet, the panorama trail is the perfect way to catch up. The "Stand" is one of the region's beacons: the highest point on the plateau offers a magnificent panoramic view of the entire Upper Valais and twelve four-thousand-metre peaks.

name: Sentiero Lago di Lugano
description: Those who have hiked these nine stages know the Sottoceneri through and through: from the pre-Alpine mountains to the Mediterranean shores, from mountain huts to grottos surrounded by vineyards, the Sottoceneri presents itself in all its diversity.

name: Oberaar Trail
description: This impressive mountain hike around the headwaters of the river Aare connects the Grimsel Pass with the Oberaarsee lake. With two self-operated cable cars, this excursion is suitable for the whole family.

name: Weg der Schweiz, Stage 2/4
description: Through cool rock galleries and over long wooden footbridges, you proceed along a steep forested hillside on the shore of Lake Uri. With the superb mountain panorama always in view, several river deltas tempt you in for a swim. In the Reuss Delta nature conservation area, fens, reed meadows and islands create valuable habitats.

name: Chemin de Raimeux
description: At an altitude of 1301 m, Mt. Raimeux is located on the border between the Canton Jura and the Bernese Jura. The views from the summit of the valley of Delémont are spectacular. When the weather is clear, even the Alps are visible in the distance. Surrounded by waterfalls and gorges, the Gore Virat creek is the jewel of the Raimeux mountain range.

name: Heinzenberger-Gratweg
description: The area's most beautiful and delightful hike over the mountain ridge that links the Heinzenberg with the Safien valley. The view of the two valleys is superb.

name: Thurweg, Stage 1/8
description: From the Thurweg trail, which is 160 kilometres long, this first stage leads along the Säntisthur, with its view of the Churfirsten, to the impressive roar of the Thur Falls. Shortly before the end of this stage at Nesslau, the river rushes down into the Giessen Falls.

name: Chemin des pyramides de Gypse
description: Thrilling hike from Bretaye around the Chaux Ronde ridge. On the way, three mountain lakes, idyllic alpine pastures, superb panoramic views of the Mont Blanc massif – and the famous gypsum pyramids near Col de la Croix.

name: Jura Crest Trail, Stage 2/16
description: After crossing Brugg's old town, the first uphill stretch to the Vier Linden country guesthouse embedded in the Jurapark, and via the forest to the ancient as well as legendary Linner Linde (linden tree). On uphill through shady forests to the Schenkenberg ruins, seen from afar, and on to Staffelegg.

name: Via Capricorn, Stage 2/3
description: The second stage leads from the Glas Pass over what was once the most important connecting route for the people of the Safien Valley. After lots of turns – known as «Stägä» – it descends to Safien Platz. Onwards through the valley, where the Walser culture has left its mark, and thence to the Turrahus.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 9/43
description: The high plateau of Plaun da Greina is an area of outstanding natural beauty with a symbolic character, an extensive water meadow, laced with small streams. The change of rock and continental microclimate are also of interest.

name: Weg der Schweiz, Stage 4/4
description: Overlooking the luminous blue Lake Lucerne and the wooded hills that surround it, the path goes up and down well-paved trails through attractive forests. The Chapel Trail near Morschach is a reminder of the rich history of the region.

name: Panorama Rundweg Thunersee
description: The Lake Thun panorama round trail is an exciting and enjoyable, several-day hike through the Bernese Oberland with majestic lake and mountain panoramas, passing historic sites and impressive caves.

name: Sentiero Cristallina
description: The Sentiero Cristallina links Bignasco in Valle Maggia with Airolo in Val Bedretto. Between them lie steep mountain slopes, a waterfall on a village outskirts, crystalline rock, Alpine lakes/reservoirs, idyllic alps and remote hamlets.

name: Chemin du vignoble, Stage 3/4
description: Sion is surrounded by a sea of vineyards that laps against the slopes of the two rocky outcrops of Valère (also known as Valeria) and Tourbillon, each crowned with castles. The terraces of grapevines in the first section of this walk are among the steepest in the world. The route takes you along a picturesque old irrigation channel, known as a “Suone”, and through winemaking villages where you can enjoy tasting opportunities.

name: Tour des Alpes Vaudoises, Stage 2/8
description: Setting off from Leysin with views of cyclists and mountain peaks, this leg leads uphill to Les Plans and onwards to a highlight of the tour: the path up to the rock face of the Tour de Famelon, surrounded by vibrant meadows. After that, there are geological structures to admire along the way. The trail leads along the Mont d’Or and onwards to Les Mosses.

name: Walliser Sonnenweg, Stage 4/4
description: Suonen (irrigation channels) and the BLS railway line accompany this stage. Impressive view of the Baltschieder viaduct. Pipes for irrigating the dry south-facing slopes line the route. Information columns on the BLS Südrampe section and Swiss Guards Museum provide fascinating information.

name: Wädenswiler-Seeuferweg
description: An excursion to the Zürichsee lake is always well worthwhile. The stretch from Horgen to Wädenswil affords particularly enchanting views over this popular body of water and the opportunity to enjoy a superb panorama.

name: Hundwiler Höhi
description: The Hunwiler Höhe is a popular hiking destination. Hikers can enjoy a splendid view from the Alpstein to Lake Constance from the summit of the pyramid-shaped elevation. Just as well known, as the mountain is the restaurant at its summit, where various specialties await the hungry hiker.

name: Sentiero Salèi e Pizzo Zucchero
description: A scenic hike through the wildest valley in the Lake Maggiore region. Enjoy the Onsernone Valley's tranquillity on old paths. Dense forests, waterfalls and hidden rustici line the route. The views extend over the deep valleys to Lake Maggiore.

name: Reiatweg
description: In the far north of Switzerland, this route snakes its way through the hilly landscape that typifies the region, past green meadows, vineyards and forests. The vista encompasses the Alpine chain and the Hegau landscape in Germany with its characteristic volcanic cones.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 1/29
description: The climb to the health resort of Heiden (Henri Dunant Museum) and to Kaienspitz is rewarded by extensive views of the Bodensee and to Alpstein. Then via Rehetobel down to Chastenloch and up to Trogen, a village where provincial assemblies were once held.

name: Appenzeller Weg, Stage 1/3
description: The fertile Rhine plains and Paspels bathing lake lie between the Rankweil fortified church and the Blatten hilltop castle in Oberriet. From Hirschensprung to Appenzell, the old pilgrimage path is lined with chapels, shrines and small pilgrimage churches.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 32/33
description: A level path with far-ranging views leads across the fields east of Lake Zurich and past various chapels and bridges. In the Middle Ages, the Linth Plain was a lake and later a swamp until about 200 years ago. Today, renaturation efforts are underway in the area.

name: Giro lungolago attorno al Monte Caslano
description: This path leads along the shores of Lake Lugano and in two sections along Monte Caslano. In addition to winding alleys and the lively piazza of Caslano, spectacular views of the straits of Lavena Ponte Tresa and Italy beckon.

name: ViaRhenana, Stage 3/10
description: A level path along the banks of the Rhine with natural riverside areas, past the Wagenhausen Propstei church and St. Katharinental Monastery and Alt Paradies; through the Schaarenwald nature reserve with its historic fortifications and on to Schaffhausen.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 10/20
description: From Andermatt the hike continues to Hospental, a typical mountain-pass village with refuge shelters, a customs post and guest houses. The route then leads along part of the cobbled post coach road dating from 1830 and the old pack-animal trail up to the pass to the Hospiz (hostel).

name: Via Engiadina, Stage 6/12
description: The leisurely hike proceeds alongside the ice-blue Inn River in the narrow valley bottom. The river winds through the Lower Engadine between huge mountain ranges. On tapered paths, past rock faces and through old coniferous forests, you will come across the ruins of Rohan Castle and the former execution site of Fuorcha.

name: ViaSett, Stage 2/6
description: South of Lenzerheide is the entrance gate to Parc Ela, the largest nature park in Switzerland. You cross meadows full of flowers to the Son Cassian chapel in the mountain village of Lenz, once a transport cooperative on the Septimer Trail. You continue on to the Carolingian church of Mistail near Tiefencastel.

name: Nationalpark-Panoramaweg, Stage 4/7
description: This tour begins and ends at the Ofen Pass road, enters the National Park and leads to the peak area of Munt la Schera, which has been flattened by the glacier. The views range far across the reservoir, Livigno valley and the Bernina group. Alpine pastures, forests of stone pine and scree gullies are a frequent sight on this tour.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 2/29
description: From Trogen (AR) over two gentle hills with wonderful views of the Säntis, the city of St.Gallen, Bodensee and the undulating Appenzell region, to the wide valley basin of Appenzell with its richly-adorned «citizens' houses».

name: Züri Oberland-Höhenweg, Stage 4/4
description: The hike's first part runs on the hillcrest and the border with Toggenburg. The panoramic views in any direction over the Zurich Oberland and the Alpine chain are fantastic. Parallel to the Jakobsweg, the trail continues to Rapperswil with its striking castle on Lake Zurich.

name: St. Galler Brückenweg
