description: This circular tour has impressive views of the Aletsch Glacier, the biggest glacier in the Alps, and the 4,000-metre peaks of Valais, making it the perfect hike for nature lovers. After Chatzulecher, you will come particularly close to the ice.

name: ViaUrschweiz, Stage 1/2
description: Isleten is an idyllic village on Lake Urn, and Gitschenen a unique sunny mountain terrace surrounded by Switzerland’s steepest wild haymaking terrain. Isenthal is located in between these two. This is an exciting hike on old paths up into the mountains.

name: Breccaschlund-Panoramaweg
description: Hollowed out by glaciers, the wild landscape of the Breccaschlund is both fascinating and mysterious. A circular walk, technically quite simple, leads from the Riggisalp, which overlooks the Schwarzsee, to the foot of some imposing cliffs. The return to the valley is punctuated with Alpine restaurants.

name: Circuito Dongio-Motto
description: The circuit is located in the southern part of the municipality of Acquarossa, in the middle of the Valle di Blenio, a flat expanse surrounded by impressive rough and jagged reliefs with emotional impact: a particular atmosphere that unites noteworthy natural and cultural qualities.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 10/32
description: Delightful hike along the River Aare, first through urban areas, then through one of Switzerland’s loveliest river landscapes. The renaturation of the river banks has brought great benefit. Worb Castle is seen from afar but is not open to the public.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 7/20
description: The stage from the sugar-producing town of Aarberg to Frauenkappelen is characterised by reservoirs, a power plant and nature reserves. Mostly along or above the wide course of the Aare, you reach Lake Wohlen and finally, via the wooded slopes, the village of Frauenkappelen a little above this.

name: Bodensee-Uferweg
description: The route from Kreuzlingen along the shores of the Bodensee to Romanshorn gives you a true holiday feeling. The entire stretch affords imposing views of and around the international fresh-water lake.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 3/20
description: The first thing to do is conquer the seemingly insurmountable Combe Grède gorge. Ladders and well-secured paths take you to the Jura heights of the Chasseral with a view of the Three-Lakes countryside and the Alpine chain. A pleasant descent through pastures and forests leads down to the tranquil Jura village of Nods.

name: Rheintaler Höhenweg, Stage 5/6
description: Setting off from the highest holiday resort in Toggenburg and featuring the highest point along the Rheintaler Höhenweg route, you will pass through highland moors and a forest reserve, enjoying glorious views of the Rhine Valley and the surrounding mountains along the way. After taking a break at an Alpine dairy, with some Alpine cheese and an Alpine lake, you will hike through multiple forests and meadows. The destination is Berghaus Malbun hotel restaurant, boasting views of Lake Constance.

name: Oberdorf-Grenchen-Waldrandweg
description: This leisurely hike from Oberdorf to Grenchen along the edge of the forest offers lovely views. One of the highlights is the Lommiswil quarry which is littered with dinosaur tracks.

name: Kerenzerberg Römerweg
description: In the footsteps of the Romans, the tour leads from Näfels over Kerenzerberg to Mühlehorn. Testimony of the times let hikers' thoughts stray to worlds of a bygone age while at the same time, the Churfirsten mountain range and the deep-blue Lake Walensee are within sight.

name: ViaValtellina, Stage 6/8
description: From the Bernina Pass up to Alp Grüm, with views into Val Poschiavo. Then descent from Alp Grüm along a historic pack-mule track to the urban charm of Poschiavo. Visit to the glacier mills at Cavaglia.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 26/32
description: The middle section of the Strada alta is considered to be the most pleasing and attractive. There are barely any altitude differences, it is mostly natural ground surfaces, and the peaks of the Leventina on the right are constantly in view. Chapels and churches enable contemplation and enjoyment of art.

name: Senda Scuol–Samnaun, Stage 1/2
description: Over flower-filled meadows, with wonderful views along the sunny slopes of the Engiadina bassa, before turning into the wild, forested Val Sinestra, past historic buildings, climb to the scenic Fimberpass, the pass to the Heidelberger Hut.

name: Leiternweide-Hängebrückenweg
description: On this diverse hike, ruins allow you a glimpse of the past, a bridge at a dizzying height will make you hold your breath and cave explorers hearts' will skip a beat. A hike right in the middle of beautiful, intact nature.

name: Alter Zügenweg
description: The historic path leads high above the striking Zügen Gorge, with views of the surrounding peaks and the Landwasser mountain river, which finds its way through the narrow gorge. The hike offers variety in every respect for families, those interested in culture, nature enthusiasts and leisure hikers.

name: Züri Oberland-Höhenweg, Stage 3/4
description: Enjoyable, varied paths follow the hillcrest, offering sweeping views over the moraine landscape to Lake Constance and the edge of the Alps with the Säntis. Following the cantonal border of Zurich and St. Gallen, the trail heads south. Beautiful beech trees and hospitality enrich the hike.

name: Gratweg Stoos
description: Renowned as one of Switzerland's finest high trails: the ridge path linking the Klingenstock and Fronalpstock peaks, with its many flights of steps. It affords views of more than ten Swiss lakes and countless Alpine peaks in Central Switzerland.

name: Obwaldner Höhenweg, Stage 5/6
description: The hiking trail along the Obwalden mountain flank of Huetstock, Nünalphorn and Widderfeldstock leads past alpine huts, over pastures and through small forests towards the Storegg pass. It offers beautiful views of the wild landscape of the Melchtal valley. After crossing the pass, you can take the Eggen cable car back down.

name: Zauberwasser-Weg Grächen
description: Dive into the specially created «Magical Water» experience: this easy trail with various stations and elements promises fun and relaxation for the whole family along the parallel irrigation channels of Eggeri and Chilcheri.

name: Obwaldner Höhenweg, Stage 2/6
description: This scenic walk in the Prealps leads through the Glaubenberg moorlands across the Glaubenberg Pass. Continuing over the Sattel Pass and Glaubenbielen Pass, you will be greeted by the panoramic views of Lungern-Schönbüel. At the end, it is worth taking a detour to the summit of the Höch Gumme, which boasts spectacular views of Lake Brienz below.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail
description: The Alpine Panorama Trail from Bodensee to Lac Léman promises many views of Alpine peaks as well as of the Mittelland and Jura. The route leads through the traditional agricultural landscape of the Alpine foothills, still dominated by milk and cheese production.

name: Via Alpina, Stage 12/20
description: The sunny terrace of Mürren lies directly opposite the Eiger, Mönch &Jungfrau. The trail leads on via Alpine pastures, vantage points such as Bryndli and sturdy huts such as the Rotstockhütte to the Sefinenfurgge, the impressive pass into the Kiental.

name: Schönriederweg
description: This route begins in the charming village of Saanenmöser and leads to the chalet village of Schönried. The intact nature of the enchanting landscape seen along this tranquil path is reminiscent of an typical Swiss picture postcard.

name: Sarnersee-Uferweg
description: Engelberg – a well-known and popular excursion destination. This round tour leads from the impressive monastery to the picturesque River Aa and constantly affords wonderful views of idyllic rural landscapes and the spectacular mountain panorama.

name: ViaBerna, Stage 17/20
description: Once again, you go down into a deep U-shaped valley. On the way to the Hasli Valley, the imposing Rychenbach Falls will surprise you before the steep stage to Zwirgi. You cross the Aare in Willigen. You then have to climb up the rock face again via a narrow path, up to the spa resort of Hasliberg Reuti.

name: Via Capricorn, Stage 1/3
description: From the mountain village of Wergenstein, the first stage leads over mountain pastures and alpine slopes to the Carnusa Pass. There are always ibexes to be seen along this stretch. After passing the turquoise Lai da Scotga, or Scottish Tarn, the trail continues to the Glas Pass.

name: Jakobsweg Graubünden, Stage 9/19
description: This stage starts in Davos Dorf and leads to Schatzalp first of all. From there, you continue across the historic Strela Pass, which was once settled by the Walser people. A challenging rocky descent leads down into the valley to the Walser settlement of Dörfji. The destination is the homely Grisons mountain village of Langwies.

name: Sentiero Lago di Lugano, Stage 4/9
description: From the small village of Medeglia, you hike through birch forests, moorlands and a former military zone to Alpe Davrosio. A picturesque mountain trail leads to the viewpoint at Motto della Croce. One hike ends and another stage begins at the beautiful Capanna Monte Bar mountain hut.

name: Mittelbünden-Panoramaweg, Stage 2/2
description: The first stop along this route is Alp Medergen, a former Walser Alp with a mountain tavern. After that, the path narrows to a mountain trail with the “Tritt” as a main landmark. At the end of this leg, you can enjoy views of Davos far below.

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 22/29
description: With the mighty Moléson mountain before you and the town of Gruyères behind you, you will climb towards the Plan-Francey middle station. Passing along the northwestern slopes of the Moléson, this leg ends after descending into the forested pre-Alpine resort of Les Paccots.

name: Zürichsee-Rundweg, Stage 4/10
description: The mountain stage of the Lake Zurich circuit takes you steadily upwards from Richterswil to the viewing point at Etzel, where you can take in a panoramic vista of the whole lake and more than 250 majestic peaks. The route then passes through forests and fields back to sea level in Pfäffikon SZ.

name: ViaJacobi, Stage 11/33
description: The stage from Spiez to Wattenwil winds through a tranquil landscape, passing several lakes against the backdrop of the mighty Stockhorn mountain range. Other highlights along the way include the 1,000-year-old churches on the shores of Lake Thun, various vineyards, Strättligburg Castle and Amsoldingen’s impressive Romanesque church.

name: Chemin de Mont-Soleil
description: This hike combines nature and innovation. On the heights of Mont-Soleil, above the valley of Saint-Imier and at the gateway to the Franches Montagnes, it offers magnificent views of the typical wooded pastures. The trail follows a part of the Sentier des Monts dedicated to renewable energies.

name: Chemin des Crêtes des Franches-Montagnes
description: A hike on the Franches-Montagnes plateau, alternating between ridges, wooded pastures, traditional hamlets and magnificent views of the Jura mountains. The wind turbines of Le Peuchapatte and Mont-Crosin in the background will spice up your hike.

name: Zürichsee-Rundweg, Stage 1/10
description: From the lake to the River Sihl: the lakeside circuit starts on Bürkliplatz, the dock that affords majestic views over the water and onwards all the way to the Alps. You begin by walking along the shore past Mythenquai to the Landiwiese park. Not long after, you pass through Wollishofen and reach the Sihl by crossing over the Entlisberg hill. The path then follows the river as far as Adliswil.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 3/43
description: This hike starts from the Walser settlement of Alp Flix amid high moorland, taking you out of Parc Ela. After the former manganese mining area near Parsettens, you follow a lovely high-level path below the peak of Pizza Grossa. A gravel road descends to Savognin and back into the country's largest nature park.

name: ViaRhenana, Stage 7/10
description: Between Schwaderloch and Rheinsulz, this widely varied section culminates on the forested northern slope of the Tafeljura mountains, with splendid views over the Rheintal valley. Particularly attractive: Koblenz with its four large historic bridges.

name: Au fil du Doubs
description: This hike does full justice to its name. The trail leads from Les Brenets near La Chaux-de-Fonds to St. Ursanne, almost always alongside the River Doubs and crossing the Doubs Regional National Park from west to east.

name: Grenzpfad Napfbergland, Stage 6/6
description: The high-level hike on the narrow ridge between the Brienzer Rothorn and the Wilerhorn offers sensational views of the high-mountain panorama and turquoise-coloured Lake Brienz. The trail then descends steeply along grassy or rocky slopes. With a bit of luck, you might spot a family of ibex.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 18/32
description: A section focusing on the Stanserhorn, which you almost circle. The Winkelried Memorial is found in Stans. The Swiss hero reputedly threw himself onto the enemies’ pikes at the Battle of Sempach in 1386 to open up a breach for the confederates.

name: ViaSbrinz, Stage 5/5
description: A demanding hike from Goms over the 2479-metre Griespass to Italy’s Val Formazza. A stage with varying Alpine landscapes, characterized by the history of the migrant Walser people and their relationship with their former homeland.

name: ViaGottardo, Stage 17/20
description: Over old, stony trails in the forest south of Tesserete, you reach the forest church of San Bernardo. Magnificent views of the lake and the surrounding mountain landscape open up. Past orange trees and vines, the route continues between old walls and modern buildings to the lakeshore in Lugano.

name: Linth-Uferweg
description: The route in Canton Glarus takes you from Schwanden to Netstal, through a broad and open valley surrounded by lush greenery and rugged mountain scenery. A route offering pure tranquillity and relaxation.

name: Kärpfbrugg-Rundweg
description: This scenic walk through Freiberg Kärpf, Europe's oldest wildlife reserve, leads across the 50 meter wide Kärpf bridge and along the Garichti lake back to Mettmen.

name: Appenzeller Weg, Stage 2/3
description: The main street in Appenzell, the old Reichsstrasse to Gontenbad, the Barfussweg on mossy soil to Jakobsbad and the Besinnungsweg (path of contemplation) leading through Alpine pastures and woodlands offer a rich variety of hiking experiences. Urnäsch beckons with its Museum of Appenzeller Traditions.

name: Alpine Passes Trail, Stage 35/43
description: The gentle hike through the Val Ferret valley leads across meadows, through forests, into small chalet villages and along the river. On the final ascent, magnificent views of the stretch you just covered in the dead-straight valley open up. The lake of picturesque Champex reflects the wild, forested mountain landscape.

name: Sound Trail
description: The Toggenburger Klangweg (sound trail) offers a very special kind of musical treat. The panorama path starts on Alp Sellamatt and combines amazing experiences with a stunning landscape. An exciting route for curious nature lovers.

name: Sentiero del Monte San Giorgio
description: Monte San Giorgio is a UNESCO World Heritage Site because of the fossil finds from the Triassic Period. These are on exhibit in the museum of Meride. Other highlights: the archaeological park in Tremona-Castello, the panoramic views from the summit, lovely Alp Brusino and the studio of local painter Fiorello Fiorini.

name: Schanfigger Höhenweg, Stage 1/6
description: The stage takes you on narrow paths through ravines and forests, past the source of the famous Passugger water. On the high plateau at Tschiertschen, you have a far-reaching view over the Schanfigg, with its scattered alms and Alpine meadows.

name: Sentier des Toblerones
description: There's no chocolate along the Toblerone Trail. It's actually an educational route that focuses on history, following a defensive line set up in the second world war between the Jura peaks and Lake Geneva. Well over 3,000 triangular tank traps resemble the "peaks" on a Toblerone bar – hence the name.

name: Schaffhauser Grenzweg
description: This section combines Europe's largest waterfall with Switzerland's largest continuous wine-growing area. As you hike from one boundary stone to the next, geology and history are the key themes. Along the way: the "Grey Stone" at boundary stone no. 67, and the ruins of Radegg Castle.

name: Trans Swiss Trail, Stage 11/32
description: Typical Emmental landscape starting above Worb: long rolling hills and steep gullies. Fantastic views of the Alps and Jura. The Gotthelf-Stube, a tiny museum on Swiss author Jeremias Gotthelf is found in the old part of Lützelflüh.

name: Swiss Tour Monte Rosa
description: Powerful combination: the Balfrin high-level trail from Sass-Fee to Grächen and the Europaweg trail from Grächen to Zermatt form the «Swiss Tour Monte Rosa». Three-day panoramic hike with stunning views of the icy 4000-m mountains of Saastal and Mattertal.

name: Bonfol Km 0
description: The focus of this hike is “Kilometre Zero“, the beginning of the World War I battlefront which extended from the Swiss border to the North Sea. In the forest, you can find the remainders of barriers, look-out posts and bunkers. The path crosses and re-crosses the border several times.
itinerary: Combe Guerri–Prés du Largin–Bannholz–Etang du Milieu

name: Promenade du Littoral de Morges
description: The route leads through the lively old town of Morges, the Parc de l'Indépendance and then past the castle to the picturesque harbour. With an impressive view of the lake and the mountain panorama with the Mont Blanc as a backdrop, the route continues along the lakeshore to Préverenges.

name: Chemin du Jura bernois, Stage 1/4
description: The trail leads across wide pastures and past ancient trees over the ridge areas of the Moron. Gravel paths and drystone walls run in a dead straight line across the hilly landscape of the Jura. Moron Tower offers a spectacular view of the Vosges, the Black Forest and across the Alps (temporarily closed).

name: Alpine Panorama Trail, Stage 9/29
description: A very scenic stage in the heart of the Zug region. Across high moors, past countless cherry orchards, the vantage point at the Brunegg restaurant and the pretty St. Verena chapel, you reach the town of Zug.

name: Toggenburger Höhenweg, Stage 4/6
description: The landscape shifts from mountains to the hilly terrain of central Toggenburg. Past the Regelstein viewpoint and the Ricken Pass village, the route goes uphill again to the Rotstein ridge. The last section calls for a leisurely stroll to your destination for this leg in Chrüzegg.
